definition: Tracking body or object poses consistently across video frames, combining per-frame estimation with temporal association.
details: Tracking body or object poses consistently across video frames, combining per-frame estimation with temporal association.

explainer.lead: Pose tracking keeps a body's or object's pose consistent over an entire video rather than judging each frame in isolation. It matters because per-frame estimates flicker or swap identities without temporal association.

tiers.eli5: Like following a dancer on screen frame by frame: you recognise it's still the same dancer, in a new position, rather than a new person every instant.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine a per-frame pose estimator with a temporal association step that links detections across frames; a common pitfall is identity switches or jitter when occlusions break the association.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, tracking defines poses across frames by combining per-frame estimation with temporal association; no single formula, and robustness depends on how association is solved under occlusion and motion.

explainer.example: In a workout video, the tracker keeps the same person's skeleton labelled consistently as they move in front of another person, instead of relabelling joints each frame.
